headline: Sensex drops 570 points as heavy foreign selling and global economic cues drag market down

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign investors sold Indian stocks en-masse, leading to massive capital outflows.
Global bond rout deepened alongside surging crude oil prices, pressuring the Rupee to a two-month low.
Global rate hike concerns sparked foreign portfolio outflows from emerging markets.
Nifty Auto slipped 3% while asset management company stocks faced rough waters.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 570 points while Nifty 50 closed around the 22,422 mark.
Indian share benchmarks logged their longest weekly losing run in 25 years.
September GST revenue rose to ₹2.03 lakh crore, though domestic sources share fell to an all-time low.
Rs 9 lakh crore of investor wealth was wiped out during market sharp declines.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices fell sharply with Sensex dropping over 570 points as equity markets recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years.
Foreign institutional investors sold heavily en-masse while rising crude oil prices and global bond yields pushed the rupee to a two-month low.
On the corporate front, NTPC posted a 13% growth in Q2 power generation, while PB Fintech shares fell dramatically below their 2021 IPO price.
